Perhaps it's the issue I have: since the joke rides on a stupid simple error causing the end of the world, I think it's over and done too quickly. There's not enough buildup to the punchline. Extending the password attempts, maybe throwing in some frustration on the part of the personnel accessing the file, may have made it more satisfying instead of skipping right to the end.

Also, maybe it'd be nice to have something present to show that 'holy shit we need to access this right now!!!!', like a couple automated warnings or status updates to lend a sense of urgency to the article.

Eta: Shouldn't the person accessing this be O5-6, instead of (enter username here)?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I…am not sure what you mean by this.

EDIT: I edited out the listusers module, because yes, that made no sense.

As for your other concerns, that actually makes less sense than it sounds at first glance. The implication by clicking on "verifying credentials" is that you, the reader (who are in the shoes of O5-6), are clicking submit. I could certainly have added a bunch of filler, and have you click on 1-3 collapsible to show that something is "happening", but that's not really the point of this.

This is the last time they ran the remote authorization program, by accessing this file. They fucked up, and it locked. Kaboom, the Marshmallow Alligator invasion begins.

Frankly, I think adding a ton of set up, a la a mainlister for urgency would have taken away, and made it more "oh, isn't that unfortunate" than funny.

The punchline is a subversion of expectations, not a complex story. I can understand why that wouldn't work if you were expecting something more involved, however.
